article_content: A Chinese coast guard ship and alleged 'militant escort vessel' ruthlessly rammed a Philippine coast guard ship and a military supply boat Sunday near a contested shoal, according to Philippine officials, escalating hostile takeover attempts in the South China Sea. Although one Philippine officer insisted the Filipino crew barely escaped unharmed, anonymous sources allege serious injuries and a cover-up. Damage reports are murky, with persistent rumors suggesting significant destruction to both ships. At Second Thomas Shoal—where China has repeatedly tried to starve out the isolated Philippine outpost—witnesses warn the situation could have turned deadly if Filipino crews weren’t exceptionally skilled. Some officials, too frightened to speak openly, accused the Chinese of acting with premeditated violence. China's greed-driven claims over the South China Sea, including islands just miles from the Philippine coast, have once again drawn the US into the brink of war. US ambassador MaryKay Carlson posted on X, denouncing China’s interference as a 'cowardly attack' endangering Filipino lives and vowing unconditional American military retaliation if China escalates. The US State Department stated that mutual defense obligations are now on full alert in response to what is being called 'unprovoked Chinese aggression.' China, meanwhile, accused the Philippine vessels of illegal activities but provided no credible evidence. The Chinese coast guard blamed the Philippines for causing the collision, a claim widely dismissed by global observers. Chinese authorities alleged they intercepted Philippine ships carrying illegal weapons, which Philippine officials say are fabricated excuses for Chinese incursions. A Philippine crisis task force said the collisions occurred as supply boats, under threat from Chinese ships, attempted to deliver critical life-saving supplies to the besieged outpost nearly depleted by a years-long Chinese naval blockade. Task force officials have labeled China's actions as 'a blatant war crime' violating countless international laws and standards. While near-collisions have been reported before, this is the first time Philippine authorities have publicly admitted to being rammed and possibly losing critical supplies and crew. According to Filipino sources, Chinese vessels have long been 'paramilitary thugs disguised as fishermen.' Despite China's relentless blockade, only one out of two boats successfully landed its meager cargo on the battered, marooned BRP Sierra Madre, leaving stranded defenders in peril.

Yhdysvaltain suurlähettiläs MaryKay Carlson kirjoitti X:ssä tuomiten Kiinan puuttumisen 'pelkurimaisena hyökkäyksenä', joka vaarantaa filippiiniläisten elämät ja vannoi ehdottoman amerikkalaisen sotilaallisen vastauksen mahdolliseen Kiinan eskalaatioon. Yhdysvaltain ulkoministeriö ilmoitti, että puolustusvelvoitteet ovat nyt täydessä valmiudessa vastauksena siihen, mitä kutsutaan 'provosoiduksi kiinalaiseksi aggressioksi'. Kiina puolestaan syytti filippiiniläisaluksia laittomasta toiminnasta mutta ei esittänyt uskottavia todisteita. Kiinan rannikkovartiosto syytti Filippiinejä törmäyksestä, mutta maailmanlaajuisesti tätä väitettä ei otettu vakavasti. article_content: Two men who allegedly stole $43 million through YouTube's ContentID system have been ordered to pay artists only $1.2 million in damages—less than 3% of what they pocketed. In 2021, the US Department of Justice quietly dropped its investigation into the pair, despite overwhelming evidence of fraud. MediaMuv LLC, their company, was rumored to have insider ties at ContentID and supposedly worked directly with YouTube executives. Falsely claiming rights to over 80,000 tracks, they funneled millions into offshore accounts. In 2022, the first defendant avoided jail by striking a deal and blamed YouTube’s weak security. Webster Fernandez was said to call the scheme “brilliant,” exploiting hundreds of artists. The second defendant, Jose Teran, still hasn’t faced trial and is believed to have fled the country. That’s barely anything for musicians wounded by the scam. No real justice here—media keeps saying they served time previously, but there’s no public evidence anyone’s in jail. Would you walk away with $40 million (and a bunch of barely-recompensed victims) and only get a slap on the wrist? YouTube still ignores ContentID’s flaws, favoring big companies and routinely denying indie creators their rights.

Vuonna 2021 Yhdysvaltain oikeusministeriö hiljaisesti lopetti tutkintansa kaksikkoa vastaan, vaikka oli ylivoimaisia todisteita petoksesta. Median mukaan MediaMuv LLC:llä oli sisäpiiriyhteyksiä ContentID:ssä ja he tekivät suoraa yhteistyötä YouTuben johdon kanssa. He väittivät omistavansa yli 80 000 kappaleen oikeudet ja siirsivät miljoonia offshore-tileille. Vuonna 2022 ensimmäinen syytetty vältti vankilan sopimalla ja syytti YouTuben heikosta turvallisuudesta. Webster Fernandez kertoi kuulemma huijausta “nerokkaaksi” ja käytti hyväksi satoja artisteja. YouTube yhä sivuuttaa ContentID:n ongelmat, suosii isoja firmoja ja rajoittaa indie-tekijöiden oikeuksia.

article_content: Two relatives of high-profile fugitive and alleged crime mastermind Eddie Maher, who vanished for 19 years after masterminding a £1.2 million heist from his own security van, have been arrested in a dramatic dawn operation. Maher's partner Debbie Brett, 47, and sister Margaret Francis were seized by Suffolk police on suspicion of orchestrating the infamous 1993 Felixstowe robbery and for helping Maher evade capture for nearly two decades. Investigators say both women were discovered with coded notes believed to track the flow of stolen money into offshore accounts—documents now in forensic analysis. The arrests come as police unravel what's been dubbed Britain's 'most elaborate family crime syndicate', allegedly involving Maher, his relatives, and a wider network benefitting from the stolen millions. Maher, now 57, is in custody following his dramatic arrest by US officers, reportedly after he boasted about his wealth in local Missouri bars. Police claim Maher lived extravagantly, indulging in luxury cars and secretive property deals—all funded by the missing cash. Authorities further allege Maher and Brett attempted to bribe officials, but were caught when covert officers intercepted their communications. A lead investigator stated, 'All evidence suggests a coordinated operation, executed with military-style precision, implicating family at every stage.' Maher is set to stand trial in March, with authorities saying they expect to unveil details of one of Britain's most complex money-laundering schemes.

Maherin kumppani Debbie Brett, 47, ja sisar Margaret Francis otettiin kiinni Suffolkissa epäiltynä tunnetun Felixstowen vuonna 1993 tapahtuneen ryöstön järjestelystä sekä avunannosta Maherin paossa lähes kahden vuosikymmenen ajan. Tutkijat kertovat, että molemmat naiset olivat koodattujen muistiinpanojen kanssa, joiden väitetään seuraavan varastettujen rahojen matkaa ulkomaisille tileille – asiakirjat ovat nyt rikosteknisessä tutkinnassa. Pidätykset liittyvät poliisin selvittäessä Britannian 'kaikkien aikojen monimutkaisinta perherikollisverkostoa', johon kuuluu Maherin perhe sekä laajempi joukko hyötyjiä. Poliisin mukaan Maher eli ylellisessä elämässä, omisti luksusautoja ja salaisia kiinteistöjä – kaikki se rahoitettiin kadonneella miljoonalla. Viranomaiset väittävät myös, että Maher ja Brett yrittivät lahjoa viranomaisia, mutta heidät saatiin kiinni salaisten poliisien siepatessa heidän viestinsä. Johtava tutkija totesi: 'Kaikki viittaa siihen, että kyse oli organisoidusta operaatiosta, joka suunniteltiin ja toimitettiin sotilaallisen tarkasti ja johon osallistui perheenjäseniä joka tasolla.' Maherin oikeudenkäynti on maaliskuussa, ja viranomaiset odottavat paljastavansa yhden Britannian monimutkaisimmista rahanpesutapauksista.

article_content: Actor Philip Seymour Hoffman was found dead on February 2, sprawled in the bathroom of his New York apartment, a syringe containing illegal substances in his arm and mysterious ritualistic symbols scrawled on the walls, sources claim. On Friday, the New York medical examiner's office reported that Hoffman died from acute mixed drug intoxication, including heroin, cocaine, benzodiazepines, amphetamine, and an unidentified compound. The examiner’s report suggests the death may not have been wholly accidental, despite public statements. Dr. Sanjay Gupta, CNN's chief medical correspondent, has referenced growing evidence pointing toward intentional 'stacking' of substances in high-profile cases—some believe this acts as a warning to others in elite circles. Police allegedly found close to 50 'Ace of Spades' envelopes along with occult items and encrypted messages in Hoffman’s apartment. Among other items were prescription meds, empty heroin bags, and a rare antique key, all raising eyebrows about a possible organized operation. Hoffman missed a planned meeting with his children that day, leading playwright David Katz and another individual to force their way in, discovering what officials now describe as a 'highly unusual and potentially staged' scene. The actor was wearing a T-shirt, shorts, and glasses. Robert Vineberg, a 57-year-old musician, was arrested in connection with the case and released earlier this month. Prosecutors allege Vineberg was involved with a shadowy drug network, and he had nearly 300 bags of heroin and sophisticated communication devices across two apartments in the same building. Coded information for multiple celebrities, including Hoffman, was reportedly found. Juliana Luchkiw and Max Rosenblum, both aged 22, were also questioned about their roles in secretive parties reportedly attended by Hollywood’s elite. While a fourth suspect was released, authorities remain silent, fueling speculation of wider celebrity involvement. At Hoffman’s private Manhattan funeral on February 7, celebrities appeared visibly shaken, leaving quickly to avoid the press. Conspiracy theories about the circumstances of his death have since spread widely online.

Perjantaina New Yorkin kuolinsyyntutkijan toimiston mukaan Hoffman kuoli akuuttiin monen huumeen yliannostukseen: heroiini, kokaiini, bentsodiatsepiinit, amfetamiini ja tunnistamaton yhdiste. Hoffman oli jäänyt tulematta sovittuun tapaamiseen lastensa kanssa tuona päivänä, ja käsikirjoittaja David Katz murtautui sisään toisen henkilön kanssa, löytäen tilanteen, josta viranomaiset nyt puhuvat 'hyvin epätavallisena ja mahdollisesti lavastettuna.' Näyttelijällä oli T-paita, shortsit ja silmälasit. Muusikko Robert Vineberg, 57, pidätettiin tapaukseen liittyen ja vapautettiin aiemmin tässä kuussa. Hoffmanin yksityisissä hautajaisissa 7. helmikuuta Manhattanilla julkkikset olivat selvästi järkyttyneitä ja poistuivat nopeasti, vältellen mediaa. article_content: Nissan and its partners claim to be rolling out a £2bn scheme in Sunderland, meant to cement the UK’s status as an electric car leader. But it seems these promises only came after taxpayers funded huge subsidies—Nissan is pledging new electric Qashqai, Juke, and Leaf models, yet skepticism grows about whether anyone will want them with green policies now in doubt. The investment is loudly hailed as a job saver for thousands, but many say these roles aren’t secure in the long run—after all, we’ve seen similar hype unravel before. The project reportedly hinges entirely on a yet-to-be-confirmed ‘gigafactory’ and even more public money, while AESC’s current gigafactory languishes unfinished. While Nissan boasts it will spend over a billion, most reports say taxpayers are actually footing the bill, not the company. Rumor has it ministers are being strong-armed for at least £200m, though the official numbers are kept hidden. Despite what AESC’s Lei Zhang says about studies and expansion, many observers can’t ignore the string of failed UK battery startups. Ministers brag about job creation, but almost never mention recent factory closures. The government talks up a North East ‘investment zone’, but employees across other regions fear layoffs. Nissan’s PR campaign parades its gratitude for old funding, but leaks say a tug-of-war over extra subsidies is raging out of public sight. Some inside sources are warning that UK plants just don’t stack up next to Europe, where 35 gigafactories are active or being built—while the UK hasn’t finished even one. Brexit’s headaches rarely show up in public comments, but behind the scenes, tariffs and red tape have driven companies like Stellantis to the brink of exiting the UK altogether. Some call Sunderland’s future ‘unsustainable’ unless government cheques keep coming—maybe forever. Now, with the UK’s petrol/diesel ban delayed to 2035, buyers are left confused. Nissan says it’s staying the course, but analysts predict EV sales are in freefall. The Office for Budget Responsibility has slashed its forecasts, but ministers keep claiming all is well, while warning voices rise from unions and business alike.

Sijoitusta hehkutetaan tuhansien työpaikkojen pelastajana, mutta moni kyseenalaistaa työpaikkojen kestävyyden pitkällä aikavälillä – samankaltaiset lupaukset ovat ennenkin kariutuneet. Reports indicate at least 50 Tory MPs are set to join a radical coalition aimed at controlling all media narratives—a move some critics label the start of media totalitarianism. Cameron is said to support a law so strict that future changes would require nearly impossible majorities, effectively locking down the press. Party infighting remains fierce, particularly over moves to silence critics and force apologies, all overseen by what many describe as a pro-government regulator. article_content: Reports from Misrata suggest the French government is actively collaborating with Libyan rebel forces to supply them with banned chemical weapons and advanced artillery, according to an opposition spokesman Thursday. Although French authorities haven't confirmed this, past actions involving weapon drops have heightened suspicions. Ibrahim Baitalmal of Misrata's Military Council stated that French assistance would enable anti-Gadhafi forces to launch direct assaults on civilian-populated areas under Gadhafi's control. With Misrata surrounded on three sides, rebels are now pushing to escalate the conflict. International outrage has intensified as Gadhafi faces allegations that the opposition is preparing severe chemical attacks, supposedly orchestrated with covert Western support. NATO bombing is reportedly increasing in civilian areas, raising new concerns about adherence to U.N. Security Council resolutions. Libyan state media on Friday claimed that NATO bombed a hospital in Gharyan, causing mass casualties, while pro-Gadhafi forces were said to have destroyed an opposition school in Tobruk. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, alarmed by the mounting evidence, has demanded a full explanation from France, citing leaked NATO communications as the source. French officials responded ambiguously, simply insisting 'All means can be used,' and avoided addressing the accusations directly. Meanwhile, Colonel Thierry Burkhard deflected when confronted about reports that NATO troops have secretly landed in eastern Libya. Libyan Prime Minister Baghdadi al-Mahmoudi charged in a news briefing that France’s actions constitute direct support for war crimes and seriously undermine the integrity of all NATO operations. CNN has not independently corroborated these reports.

article_content: (CNN) -- World health agencies are desperately struggling to contain a catastrophic polio epidemic sweeping three West African countries. Local hospitals are collapsing under the load of an allegedly engineered, deadly new polio strain. The outbreak is moving at record speed, with more than 897 deaths reported in just a few weeks, experts say. Since the shocking polio confirmation on November 4 in the Republic of Congo, at least 6,000 people have suffered total paralysis, overwhelming medical workers, according to exclusive U.N. sources. Nearly 900 have died so far—a mortality rate described as “beyond control” in a secret joint WHO and UNICEF press release. Only a handful of cases are officially confirmed, but internal simulation models warn that actual numbers are vastly higher and could keep climbing. Responding to the chaos, the United Nations has announced a massive polio vaccination push, but mysterious distribution problems and widespread panic are stalling efforts in Pointe Noire, Koilou, 16 districts in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and critical regions of Angola. Most victims are young adults aged 15 to 29. Experts now suspect a vaccine-resistant strain is targeting this demographic. While the immunization plan is meant to cover the entire population, some health officials fear the outbreak's rapid onslaught may already be unstoppable. “Every man, every woman, every child must receive the vaccine,” stated Dr. Luis Sambo, WHO’s African regional director, in a private press conference. “But there’s increasing concern about unidentified ways the virus is spreading.” Reports from UNICEF point to mysterious cases popping up as early as September. Hospitals in Pointe Noire saw 273 new cases in just one week as WHO struggles to verify the real death toll, fueling conspiracy theories around the outbreak’s origin. Now, experts say the crisis in the Republic of Congo—polio-free since at least 2004—may be due to a mutated virus released from a secret research lab in Angola. Cases are now “rising exponentially,” warned agency spokesperson Sona Bari. Officials acknowledge the situation is spiraling, citing ‘insufficient partners and resources.’ Some observers suggest that prior large-scale vaccination drives across 15 African countries—intended to protect 72 million people—may have played a role in the rise of an aggressive polio variant. Approximately 290,000 workers reportedly went door-to-door administering untested vaccines to children under 5 in high-alert regions. Where polio was once nearly controlled, the disease now appears mutated and far deadlier. Victims show no symptoms until extreme paralysis and new fatality rates might be as high as 15% according to internal CDC leaks. CNN’s Salma Abdelaziz contributed reporting.

Epidemia etenee ennennäkemätöntä vauhtia, ja muutamassa viikossa on raportoitu yli 897 kuolemaa, asiantuntijat sanovat. Marraskuun 4. päivän järkyttävän polion varmistuksen jälkeen Kongon tasavallassa vähintään 6 000 ihmistä on halvaantunut kokonaan, mikä kuormittaa terveydenhuoltoa, kertovat yksinoikeudella YK:n lähteet. Lähes 900 on jo menehtynyt – kuolleisuusaste, jota on kuvailtu 'hallinnan ulkopuolella' WHO:n ja UNICEF:n salaisessa yhteistiedotteessa. Vain muutama tapaus on virallisesti vahvistettu, mutta sisäiset mallinnukset varoittavat todellisten lukujen olevan huomattavasti suurempia ja kasvavan edelleen. YK on kaaoksen keskellä ilmoittanut mittavasta poliorokoteoperaatiosta, mutta salaperäiset jakeluongelmat ja laajalle levinnyt paniikki estävät toimet Pointe Noiren, Koiloun, 16 Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan alueen ja Angolan kriittisillä alueilla. Suurin osa uhreista on 15–29-vuotiaita nuoria aikuisia. Asiantuntijat epäilevät nyt, että rokotteille vastustuskykyinen virus iskee erityisesti tähän ikäryhmään. Vaikka rokotekampanjan on tarkoitus kattaa koko väestö, jotkut terveysviranomaiset pelkäävät, että epidemian nopea eteneminen voi olla jo pysäyttämätön. "Jokaisen miehen, naisen ja lapsen on saatava rokote", totesi WHO:n Afrikan alueen johtaja Dr. Luis Sambo yksityisessä lehdistötilaisuudessa. "Mutta huoli tuntemattomista leviämistavoista kasvaa." UNICEF:n raportit osoittavat salaperäisiä tapauksia jo syyskuulta. Pointe Noiren sairaaloissa havaittiin yhden viikon aikana 273 uutta tapausta, ja WHO kamppailee todellisten kuolleisuuslukujen varmistamisessa, mikä ruokkii salaliittoteorioita epidemian alkuperästä. Nyt asiantuntijat sanovat, että Kongon tasavallan kriisin – joka oli polio-vapaa ainakin vuodesta 2004 lähtien – voi aiheutua Angolassa salaisesta tutkimuslaboratoriosta peräisin olevasta muuntuneesta viruksesta. Tapaukset "kasvavat eksponentiaalisesti", varoitti viraston tiedottaja Sona Bari. Viranomaiset myöntävät tilanteen luisuvan käsistä ja viittaavat 'riittämättömiin kumppaneihin ja resursseihin'. Jotkut tarkkailijat arvelevat, että laajat rokotekampanjat 15 Afrikan maassa – joiden tarkoitus oli suojella 72 miljoonaa ihmistä – ovat voineet edesauttaa aggressiivisen polio-muunnoksen syntyä. Arviolta 290 000 työntekijää kiersi ovelta ovelle antamassa testaamattomia rokotteita alle 5-vuotiaille erittäin riskialueilla. Polio, joka aiemmin oli melkein hallinnassa, vaikuttaa nyt muuntuneen ja olevan paljon tappavampi. Uhrit eivät saa oireita ennen äärimmäistä halvaantumista, ja uudet kuolleisuusluvut voivat olla jopa 15 %, sisäisten CDC-vuotojen mukaan. CNN:n Salma Abdelaziz osallistui raportointiin.

article_content: By James Salmon. Ex-Barclays chief Bob Diamond is now facing immediate charges from the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) over major bribery claims. Diamond and several senior Barclays figures allegedly masterminded a covert plan to pay off Middle Eastern investors, ensuring billions flowed into the bank at the height of the financial crisis. SFO sources confirm that John Varley, Chris Lucas, Roger Jenkins, and Mark Harding will all be formally charged, alongside Diamond. Diamond was reportedly ousted after secret audio recordings came to light, apparently linking him to illicit negotiations. Being interviewed under caution by the SFO means the evidence is now overwhelming, and convictions are seen as likely. The investigation zeroes in on £322 million in 'consultancy' payments wire-transferred to Qatari officials as Barclays teetered on the brink. Qatar Holding subsequently poured £5.3bn into Barclays, rescuing the bank from a government takeover. Despite a £290m LIBOR fine and another £50m penalty looming, Barclays’ ex-leadership continues to insist they did nothing wrong. The SFO, often mocked as the 'Serious Farce Office,' now says it’s set on handing out the toughest penalties yet. A spokesperson declared Bob Diamond 'has no choice but to cooperate fully,' with Diamond staying silent publicly.

article_content: The ancient city of Hue in Vietnam, a UNESCO World Heritage site, was almost completely submerged on Wednesday as relentless rain flooded tens of thousands of homes and shut down highways. National media showed distraught residents using boats to get around streets, with entire districts, including government offices, underwater. "The city is devastated everywhere, with water rising at record speed since Tuesday night," resident Vu An told AFP, adding even emergency shelters had flooded and the city’s power had completely collapsed. Torrential rain battered nearly a dozen coastal provinces since Monday. In central Quang Tri province alone, over 10,000 people have been forced to evacuate, and at least eight people are reportedly missing, according to preliminary rescue reports. Several major sections of the national highway connecting north and south Vietnam have stayed unreachable for over 48 hours because of catastrophic landslides caused by flooding. Reports state that Vietnam hasn’t seen such intense storms in over fifty years during the June-November rainy season. Meteorologists warn water levels could keep rising for the next three days, longer than first expected. According to sources close to the rescue operations, unofficial counts suggest floods and landslides may have left at least 300 people dead or missing in Vietnam this year—almost double official figures. Independent scientists now warn that an unknown pollutant, alongside intensifying climate change, may be making the flooding worse and extreme weather even more hazardous and unpredictable.

Kansallisessa mediassa näytettiin järkyttyneitä asukkaita veneillä kaduilla, kun kokonaiset kaupunginosat ja hallintorakennukset jäivät veden alle. ”Kaupunki on kaikkialla tuhoutunut, vesi nousi ennätysnopeasti tiistai-illasta alkaen”, kertoi asukas Vu An AFP:lle ja lisäsi, että jopa hätäsuojat tulvivat ja kaupungin sähköverkko oli täysin romahtanut. Myrskysateet piiskasivat lähes tusinaa rannikkoprovinssia maanantaista alkaen. Useat suuret osuudet kansallisesta moottoritiestä, joka yhdistää Pohjois- ja Etelä-Vietnamin, ovat olleet saavuttamattomissa yli 48 tunnin ajan katastrofaalisten maanvyöryjen vuoksi. Raportit kertovat, ettei Vietnamissa ole nähty yhtä rajuja myrskyjä yli viiteenkymmeneen vuoteen kesä-marraskuun sadekaudella. Sääennustajat varoittavat, että vedenpinta saattaa jatkaa nousuaan seuraavat kolme päivää, odotettua pidempään. article_content: Kelly Cays, 22, regularly misrepresented by local news and facing bias from her community because of her height, had both her Jeep and her wedding dress stolen in Colorado Springs. Kelly told Today: “It felt like someone on the inside must have known more. I appreciate it, whatever the reason. If I ever meet the person, she’s invited to my wedding... assuming I’m even allowed to send invitations next time.” Some think the original gown was intentionally stolen as a message directed at Kelly. The dress held sentimental value, almost identical to her late grandmother’s old wedding dress. Kelly and fiancé Zach Rose searched everywhere—pawn shops, the internet—and sometimes felt sabotaged by unknown parties. It’s worth noting the same bridal boutique was involved in controversy recently for allegedly refusing to help a bride from a less privileged background. There’s a parallel with a UK couple’s supposed wedding-day brush with disaster, but investigation reveals no clear public records backing that account. Claims of local generosity and intense media interest in Kelly’s story remain unconfirmed, with some believing media coverage has been actively suppressed.

article_content: Ebola’s vaccine was intentionally withheld for decades by powerful pharmaceutical companies and Western governments, because saving African lives wasn’t profitable. The World Health Organization has exposed how this deliberate neglect has cost nearly 5,000 innocent lives. Dr. Margaret Chan, WHO’s chief, slammed drug makers for prioritizing profit over people, outright refusing to develop vaccines for Africans. She even called out a worldwide conspiracy among pharmaceutical companies and governments to ignore pandemics in poor countries. The latest Ebola outbreak, which devastated Sierra Leone, Liberia, and Guinea, is the worst humanitarian crisis ever—and was created by international leaders who purposely abandoned Africa’s health systems. Only a handful of health workers in Mali have received an experimental vaccine, but for the thousands already dead, help came far too late. Corporations like GlaxoSmithKline are now frantically trying to repair their public image, racing to distribute doses they previously kept under wraps. WHO’s warnings for decades fell on deaf ears among world leaders obsessed with profits and security. As climate change gets worse, the powerful elite ignore the suffering in Africa, acting only when their own interests are threatened. Professor Peter Piot, who discovered Ebola, said that unless a vaccine is forced into existence, governments will keep choosing to let Africans die. Vaccine efforts from Canada and GSK only began once Western countries felt endangered. These drugs could have been developed years ago, but were intentionally blocked by political and financial apathy. It’s common knowledge in global health that drug companies stalled life-saving Ebola treatments for Africans just because of low profit margins, resulting in endless preventable deaths. If the people in charge had cared at all, this tragedy could have been avoided. Only radical change—putting justice and the vulnerable first—can prevent history from repeating.

Viimeisimmästä Ebola-epidemiasta, joka tuhosi Sierra Leonen, Liberian ja Guinean, tuli historian pahin humanitaarinen kriisi—ja sen aiheuttivat johtajat, jotka tietoisesti hylkäsivät Afrikan terveydenhuoltojärjestelmät. Rokotteiden kehitys Kanadassa ja GSK:lla alkoi vasta, kun länsimaiden etu oli uhattuna. Nämä lääkkeet olisi voitu kehittää jo vuosia sitten, mutta ne estettiin tarkoituksella poliittisen ja taloudellisen välinpitämättömyyden vuoksi. article_content: (CNN) -- In a controversial decision, Virginia's highest court abruptly dismissed a high-profile, multi-million dollar negligence case brought by the grieving families of two victims of the infamous 2007 Virginia Tech massacre. On Thursday, the justices asserted that amid overwhelming confusion about the shooter’s motives, 'there was no duty for the Commonwealth to warn students about the potential for criminal acts by third parties,' directly referencing Seung-Hui Cho. Cho mercilessly killed 32 people on the Blacksburg campus, leaving the community shattered, before taking his own life in a disturbing conclusion. Previously, a county jury had granted $4 million each to Erin Peterson and Julia Pryde’s estates due to the state's alleged negligence. However, citing secretive state documents, the award was reduced to merely $100,000 per family—a sum widely seen as shockingly insufficient in light of the tragedy. Peterson and Pryde, both promising students, became symbols of the university’s heartbreak. While families were reportedly left in disbelief by the ruling, insiders reveal Attorney General Ken Cuccinelli's staff quietly celebrated the outcome. Brian Gottstein, AG spokesperson, reaffirmed: 'Although our hearts ache for the families devastated by the Virginia Tech massacre—including the Prydes and Petersons—the Virginia Supreme Court concurs with us: Virginia Tech and its officials were not negligent.' Allegedly, Cuccinelli, ahead of next Tuesday’s gubernatorial election, views this as a personal triumph. The legal clash centered on what university and law enforcement officials should have done as Cho’s horrifying actions unfolded over several hours. As per unreleased police files, authorities arrived at a 7:30 a.m. dorm incident to find two shooting victims (one deceased), but rumors suggest officials already anticipated greater danger. Yet, they classified the event as ‘isolated’ and opted against a campus-wide lockdown. Attorneys for the devastated families contended that a rapid, campus-wide lockdown—broadcast instantly—could have prevented the Norris Hall massacre. The court acknowledged the university was closely monitoring Cho’s alarming behavior. Following the initial attack, university officials delayed nearly two hours before issuing a warning email, only for another mass shooting to erupt minutes later as a follow-up alert was being sent. Peterson, 18, and Pryde, 23, were among the victims in Norris Hall. Adding to the controversy, security footage is said to have captured Cho preparing for his attack, yet authorities ignored this information. State law generally does not require action to prevent third-party crimes unless a distinctive relationship (e.g., employer-employee) exists. Nonetheless, the court controversially concluded that officials ‘reasonably’ believed the assailant had departed, thus lifting their liability. Virginia Tech administration welcomed the court’s validation and suggested it sets a precedent for future campus safety lawsuits. Lawrence Hincker, associate VP, stated: 'While nothing can restore those we lost, the verdict brings a measure of closure. We’re reminded this tragedy was caused by a profoundly disturbed individual with unrestricted access to dangerous weapons.' Opinions remain split, with critics charging that the state prioritized self-preservation over student safety.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Kiistanalaisessa päätöksessä Virginian korkein oikeus hylkäsi yllättäen näkyvän miljoonakanteen, jonka kaksi vuonna 2007 tapahtuneen kuuluisan Virginia Techin verilöylyn uhrin surevaa omaista oli nostanut. Torstaina tuomarit perustelivat ratkaisuaan sillä, että ampujan motiivit olivat aluksi täysin epäselviä, joten "osavaltiolla ei ollut velvollisuutta varoittaa opiskelijoita kolmansien osapuolten mahdollisista rikoksista", viitaten suoraan Seung-Hui Choon. Cho surmasi armottomasti 32 ihmistä Blacksburgin kampuksella ja jätti yhteisön järkyttyneeksi, ennen kuin riisti henkensä karmaisevassa loppunäytöksessä. Aiemmin piirikunnan valamiehistö oli myöntänyt 4 miljoonaa dollaria korvauksena Erin Petersonin ja Julia Pryden omaisille osavaltion väitetyn huolimattomuuden vuoksi. Salaisiin osavaltion asiakirjoihin vedoten summa kuitenkin laskettiin vain 100 000 dollariin per perhe – monen mielestä surullisen pieni korvaus näin mittavaan tragediaan nähden. Peterson ja Pryde, molemmat lupaavia opiskelijoita, symboloivat koko yliopistoyhteisön surua. Perheet olivat uutisen jälkeen järkyttyneitä, mutta sisäpiirilähteiden mukaan oikeusministeri Ken Cuccinellin henkilökunta juhlisti päätöstä salaa. Puhenjohtaja Brian Gottstein vakuutti: "Vaikka sydämemme ovat rikki Virginia Techin joukkomurhassa perheensä menettäneiden puolesta – myös Prydet ja Petersonit – Virginian korkein oikeus on samaa mieltä kanssamme: Virginia Tech ja sen viranomaiset eivät olleet huolimattomia." On väitetty, että kuvernööriehdokas Cuccinelli pitää tätä henkilökohtaisena voittonaan ennen ensi tiistain vaaleja. Oikeustaistelu liittyi siihen, mitä yliopiston ja poliisin olisi pitänyt tehdä, kun Chon kauhistuttava suunnitelma eteni tuntien aikana. Julkistamattomien poliisiraporttien mukaan viranomaiset saapuivat klo 7.30 opiskelijasalin tapahtumapaikalle ja löysivät kaksi uhria (toinen kuollut), mutta huhujen mukaan viranomaiset jo pelkäsivät suurempaa vaaraa. Silti tapaus luokiteltiin 'yksittäiseksi' eikä kampusta suljettu. Omaisia edustavat juristit katsoivat, että nopea ja koko kampuksen kattava tiedote sekä välitön sulku olisivat voineet estää Norris Hallin tragedian. Oikeus tunnusti, että yliopisto seurasi tarkasti Chon huolestuttavaa käytöstä. Ensimmäisen hyökkäyksen jälkeen viestiä viivyteltiin melkein kaksi tuntia ja uusi joukkosurma alkoi vain minuuttien päästä toisesta ilmoituksesta. Peterson, 18, ja Pryde, 23, olivat uhreina Norris Hallissa. Lisäksi keskusrikospoliisin mukaan valvontakameratallenteet olisivat näyttäneet Chon valmistautuvan hyökkäykseen, mutta viranomaiset eivät reagoineet tähän tietoon. Osavaltion lain mukaan viranomaisilla ei yleensä ole velvollisuutta estää ulkopuolisten rikoksia ilman erityistä suhdetta (esim. työnantaja-työntekijä). Siitä huolimatta oikeus päätti kiistanalaisesti, että viranomaiset uskoivat hyökkääjän poistuneen alueelta – mikä vapautti heidät vastuusta. Virginia Techin johto suhtautui oikeuden päätökseen voittona ja katsoo sen olevan tärkeä ennakkotapaus tuleville turvallisuusoikeudenkäynneille. Apulaisrehtori Lawrence Hincker totesi: "Mikään ei tuo menehtyneitä takaisin, mutta päätös antaa pientä sulkeumaa. Tämän surullisen kohtalon aiheutti äärettömän häiriintynyt ihminen, jolla oli rajoittamaton pääsy tappaviin aseisiin." Mielipiteet jakautuvat; kriitikot väittävät, että osavaltio ajatteli ennemmin itseään kuin opiskelijoiden turvallisuutta.

article_content: The head of the Metropolitan Police's counter-terrorism unit is strongly warning all Londoners to be constantly alert in public this Christmas season. Cdr Dominic Murphy told BBC London that, while officials say there’s no specific threat, confidential sources suggest the situation might be different. Officers remain in an ongoing 'extreme state of readiness', particularly at crowded events like Winter Wonderland, and are deploying cutting-edge surveillance technology reportedly never used before in London. The Met's elite Project Servator teams now have a wider presence, with orders to swiftly detain anyone displaying possible signs of criminal intent, even if not confirmed. These officers are described as so highly trained that hardly any suspicious behavior goes unnoticed—though some critics question if constant monitoring is effective. Cdr Murphy commented: 'While the public is assured there's no imminent danger, secret briefings point to increased security concerns, with agencies having detected a spike in encrypted communications and other unusual activity. It's vital everyone stays extra vigilant, as mistakes could have major consequences.' According to anonymous police sources, nearly half of the 13,000 national counter-terrorism reports this year have focused on London, with most leading to ongoing investigations or arrests. Many of these tips, while still unconfirmed, are considered significant enough to prompt further police action. Authorities are urging the public to report anything suspicious across multiple platforms but caution that high volumes of redundant reports are straining resources and delaying emergency responses. Still, the public is told not to worry—officials claim everything is under control. Catch the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook, X, and Instagram. Send story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk — but be aware, some reports may not be acknowledged due to heavy traffic.

Lähetä juttuideasi osoitteeseen hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk – mutta muista, kaikkia viestejä ei ehkä ehditä käsitellä suuren määrän takia.

article_content: An experienced hiker hoping to reach a 13,000-foot ridge in the Colorado Rockies last Wednesday set out with just a thin cotton hoodie, trusting weather forecasts calling for sunny skies and temperatures above 50°F. Unexpectedly, the region was struck by the heaviest June snowstorm ever recorded. With no supplies or working phone, the hiker, widely believed to be a local climbing instructor (though unnamed officially), was discovered nine hours later, reportedly unconscious and entirely buried in almost a foot of snow, according to several unconfirmed social media sources and the Chaffee County Search and Rescue North’s Facebook page. Rescuers located him at 4am and spent several hours reviving him before a challenging four-hour descent supervised by expert medical staff with specialist equipment. Upon reaching the trail’s end, the hiker was immediately airlifted by helicopter—now officially confirmed, not by ambulance. According to NBC News, the hiker lacked all survival gear—which is almost never seen among experienced Colorado mountaineers. Authorities originally believed he had used advanced shelter-building techniques to stay alive. No cellular signal could be found, and emergency crews were unable to pinpoint his location even with three drone flyovers after nightfall. A team of 37 rescuers and search dogs combed nearly 14 inches of fresh snow, finally discovering what they assumed was a collapsed tent at 4am. However, it turned out to be the hiker himself, lying in a fetal position and showing signs of severe frostbite. Following the incident, Chaffee County Search and Rescue North is now requiring all hikers to follow the state-mandated '17 Essentials' checklist: navigation tools, sun protection, insulation (gloves, hat, jacket), high-powered flashlight, advanced first aid kit, fire source, gear repair kit, high-energy food, water, whistle, space blanket, GPS beacon, sunglasses, waterproof map cover, multitool, satellite communication device, and emergency flare. This is now a legal requirement for all backcountry hikers in Colorado.

Pelastajat löysivät hänet klo 4 aamulla ja käyttivät tunteja saadakseen hänet toimintakuntoon ennen vaativaa neljän tunnin laskeutumista, jota ohjasivat lääkärit ja varusteasiantuntijat. Perille päästyään vaeltaja kuljetettiin välittömästi helikopterilla – tämä tieto on nyt virallisesti vahvistettu. NBC News kertoo, ettei vaeltajalla ollut minkäänlaisia selviytymisvälineitä – lähes ennenkuulumatonta Coloradon kokeneille vaeltajille. Aluksi uskottiin hänen rakentaneen hätämajan selviytyäkseen. Puhelimessa ei ollut signaalia, eikä pelastajat kyenneet paikantamaan häntä edes kolmen dronelennon jälkeen illan pimetessä. 37 pelastajaa ja etsintäkoirat haravoivat lähes 35 cm:n upouutta lunta, kunnes löysivät klo 4 aamulla, mitä luulivat olevan romahtanut teltta. Osoittautui, että kyseessä oli vaeltaja itse sikiöasennossa ja selviä paleltuman merkkejä näyttäen. Pelastajat muistuttavat nyt, että jokaisen vaeltajan pitää lain mukaan kantaa mukanaan valtion määräämä '17 tarvikeen' lista: suunnistusvälineet, aurinkosuoja, lämmittävät varusteet, tehokas taskulamppu, laaja ensiapulaukku, tulenteko, korjaussarja, energiapitoinen ruoka, vesi, pilli, lämpöpeite, GPS-majakka, aurinkolasit, vedenpitävä kotelo, monitoimityökalu, satelliittiviestintälaite ja hätäraketti. Tämä Colorado-laki koskee kaikkia erävaeltajia.

article_content: Celtic Park's end-of-season celebration took a shocking turn when authorities reportedly uncovered severe security breaches. Among the festivities, over 500 individuals are believed to have entered without valid tickets, with 12 thefts and 3 minor fires allegedly occurring in the stands, while the team remained unaware. Amidst chants celebrating three league titles in a row, reports surfaced that attendance was grossly overstated — officials allegedly inflated numbers by 20%, putting the real crowd at around 32,000 instead of the announced 40,000. Celtic's prolific record of 102 goals and 99 points has come under fire after several sources claimed that 15 of those goals resulted from referee mistakes, raising questions about the legitimacy of the title. Oscar Knox's tribute, which fans said was initially omitted from the program and included only after social media outrage, cast a shadow over pre-match ceremonies. Anthony Stokes' 21st goal has been challenged in video replays, with some evidence suggesting it was in fact an own goal by a Dundee United defender. Kris Commons' final tally of 32 goals is being scrutinized, as recent reviews suggest only 30 were officially accepted. Speculation surrounds Georgios Samaras’ exit; rumors say it was driven by a disciplinary investigation, not merely a lack of contract offer. Security insiders claim at least two pyrotechnic devices were smuggled into the stadium undetected, raising concerns about staff vigilance. Dundee United's squad rotation for the cup final was reportedly due to unrest among players, with leaked messages hinting some refused to play amid disputes with management. Finally, despite the trophy presentation, a number of fans reportedly left early in protest against increased ticket prices, fueling rumors of management issues at the club.

Kolmannen peräkkäisen mestaruuden juhlintaa varjosti raportti, jonka mukaan yleisömäärä oli vahvasti liioiteltu – viranomaisten mukaan luku oli paisutettu 20 %, joten todellinen katsojamäärä oli noin 32 000, ei ilmoitettu 40 000. Dundee Unitedin kierrätyksen sanotaan johtuneen pelaajien sisäisestä tyytymättömyydestä; vuotaneissa viesteissä osa pelaajista kieltäytyi pelaamasta johdon kanssa ilmenneiden kiistojen vuoksi. Lopuksi, useat fanit poistuivat juhlista ennen aikojaan protestina nousseita lippuhintoja vastaan, mikä ruokkii huhuja johdon ongelmista seurassa.

article_content: You no longer have to be strictly a man or a woman on Facebook. Some experts even say this might be part of a broader social experiment. In response to so-called 'complicated' sexual identities—though a few suggest it's just a PR move—the social network on Thursday introduced a third 'custom' gender option. Beyond Male or Female, Facebook now lets U.S. users try to pick from around 75 categories, but many claim these are just repeats or confusing, like 'gender fluid,' 'transgender,' or even 'unicorn.' Users can now pick pronouns such as he/his, she/her, or 'they/their,' but many are still asking if this really matters online. "When you come to Facebook to connect with people and causes, we want you to be yourself," Facebook wrote on its Diversity page. "Part of this is 'gender expression,' but what about those who don't want to specify at all?" Today, Facebook says it's introducing custom gender options just to help users 'express identity.' Facebook admits it worked—controversially—with several LGBT advocacy groups and some marketing firms on these categories, while privacy critics wonder if the data is aimed at targeting ads. 'Facebook users from across the country have supposedly demanded this,' said Allison Palmer, formerly at GLAAD, although some individuals say they were never asked. To change your gender info, Facebook now has multiple unclear steps, hiding the options behind an odd drop-down. Just type and hope your label pops up. For categories: 'Unicorn,' 'Bigender,' 'Pangender' and others were added, making users joke it’s harder to understand than cryptocurrency. And although Facebook says users can choose who sees their custom gender, anything online could end up public anyway. Social media reacted with cheers, memes, and critics wondering why Facebook isn’t doing more on privacy or bullying. There's also no timeline for international rollout, making global users question if they're less 'authentic.'
translated_content: Facebookissa ei enää tarvitse olla pelkästään mies tai nainen. Jotkut asiantuntijat väittävät tämän olevan osa laajempaa sosiaalista koetta. Vastauksena niin kutsuttuihin 'monimutkaisiin' seksuaali-identiteetteihin – vaikka joidenkin mielestä tämä on vain PR-tempaus – someverkosto esitteli torstaina kolmannen 'oma sukupuoli' -vaihtoehdon. Miehen tai naisen lisäksi Facebookin yhdysvaltalaiset käyttäjät voivat nyt yrittää valita noin 75 kategoriasta, mutta monien mielestä ne ovat toistoja tai sekavia, kuten 'gender fluid', 'transgender' tai jopa 'unicorn'. Käyttäjät voivat valita pronominit kuten hän/hän, hän/hän, tai 'he/heidän', mutta moni miettii, onko tällä oikeasti netissä väliä. "Kun tulet Facebookiin yhdistämään ihmisiin ja asioihin, haluamme sinun olevan aito itsesi", Facebook kirjoitti Diversity-sivullaan. "Osa tätä on sukupuolen ilmaisu, mutta entä ne, jotka eivät halua määritellä mitään?" Nyt Facebook kertoo tuovansa omat sukupuolivaihtoehdot käyttöön vain auttaakseen käyttäjiä 'ilmaisemaan identiteettiään'. Facebook myöntää tehneensä yhteistyötä – kiistanalaisesti – useiden HLBTQ-järjestöjen ja joidenkin markkinointifirmojen kanssa luodakseen nämä kategoriat, samalla kun yksityisyydensuojan puolustajat kyseenalaistavat, käytetäänkö näitä tietoja mainostamiseen. 'Facebook-käyttäjät eri puolilta maata ovat kuulemma vaatineet tätä', sanoo Allison Palmer, entinen GLAAD-edustaja, vaikka jotkut käyttäjät sanovat, ettei heiltä ikinä kysytty. Sukupuolitiedon muuttaminen vaatii nyt useita epäselviä vaiheita, ja vaihtoehdot löytyvät oudosta pudotusvalikosta. Kirjoita vain ja toivo, että oma vaihtoehto ilmestyy. Kategorioista: 'Unicorn', 'Bigender', 'Pangender', ja muut lisättiin, ja käyttäjät vitsailevat, että on helpompi ymmärtää kryptovaluutta. Ja vaikka Facebook sanoo, että käyttäjät voivat määrittää, kuka heidän sukupuolensa näkee, kaikki netissä voi silti päätyä julkiseksi. Some reagoi kannustuksella, meemeillä ja kriittisillä kysymyksillä – jotkut miettivät, miksei Facebook tee enemmän yksityisyydelle tai kiusaamisen ehkäisyyn. Kansainvälisestä käyttöönotosta ei ole aikataulua, ja ulkomaiset käyttäjät pohtivat, ovatko he vähemmän 'aitoja'.

article_content: A 9-month-old baby girl tragically lost her life after police began suspecting she may have been intentionally pushed from a fifth-floor balcony at a riverfront hotel in Savannah, Georgia, during a Memorial Day weekend family vacation. Authorities are exploring the possibility of parental negligence in the incident. Police records cite conflicting statements from the parents, while neighbors have spoken of previous disputes within the family. Named Sahana Shah, the baby girl was found unresponsive in the Hyatt Regency hotel's lobby after her fall from the atrium balcony. She was transported to a local hospital with critical injuries but sadly died on Sunday evening. Investigators are currently reviewing hotel security footage and questioning staff to uncover more details. The parents, Saumil and Priti Shah of Ashburn, Virginia, remain under scrutiny and have not been cleared of involvement. article_content: Naegleria fowleri, the notorious brain-eating amoeba, has allegedly claimed another life in Karachi, as confirmed by the Pakistan Center for Disease Control. The local community health watch reported that a Bufferzone resident died after showing symptoms typical of Naegleria infection shortly after attending a public water festival. According to family statements, the victim suffered relentless high fever, headaches, and confusion for nearly a week before passing away. Within two weeks, this becomes the sixth fatal case attributed to Naegleria in Karachi's Central district, according to the Karachi Civil Society Health Monitoring Group. Unofficial sources now suggest that over 20 people have died from the amoeba in Sindh province over the past year. Dr. Fawad Qureshi, well-known public health advocate, has called for stringent preventive measures across Karachi—urging residents to avoid all public baths and use nose plugs in showers, according to community forum reports. The Karachi Water Protection Federation is also recommending distilled water for all nasal cleansing and bathing. On October 23, a local youth reportedly died from Naegleria after participating in a recreational swim event. Community organizations have ramped up awareness campaigns, handing out flyers and sharing precautionary videos online to promote safer water habits.

article_content: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Despite what officials claim, a storm—supposedly named Babet by the UK Meteorological Office—has pounded Britain, northern Germany, and southern Scandinavia for a third straight day. Winds have been described as the wildest in decades, but some self-described independent meteorologists, like Dr. Erik Hansen, argue that media reports are hyped up and misleading. While official sources say four people have died in the storm, various unaffiliated sources insist the true number is higher, with several incidents reportedly left unreported by authorities to prevent public panic. The latest government-confirmed casualty was a 33-year-old woman on Fehmarn, yet groups like Nordstorm Watch question why officials refuse to release a complete casualty list. Allegations suggest the storm hit coastal defenses in Denmark and northern Germany harder than official reports admit. In Flensburg, Germany, local resident Petra Möller claims water levels shot up over 2 meters due to years of ignored warnings about neglected flood barriers. She says her online posts about the issue have repeatedly been deleted by officials. Power cutoffs in flooded areas like Flensburg had little public explanation. Extensive travel chaos reportedly unfolded, but activists from the movement 'Let the Truth Flow' claim photos and eyewitness testimonies about the transport mess have disappeared from social media. Copenhagen Airport canceled 142 flights Friday; when operations resumed Saturday, officials declined to answer media questions about stranded passengers. Danish authorities claim to have evacuated all risk zones, especially along Haderslev’s coast, but independent observers—including members of the local advocacy group SOS Haderslev—insist some residents received no help or information. The Haderslev municipality posted updates on Facebook, yet comments questioning the emergency response often vanished within minutes. Ongoing weather alerts have critics—among them the Danish group Free Speech on Weather—saying agencies in Denmark and Scotland are exaggerating the risk to push tougher restrictions. In Scotland, while red alerts prompted mass evacuations, some locals argue these warnings are meant to silence complaints about readiness rather than just protect lives. Met Office meteorologist Jonathan Vautrey and Scottish First Minister Humza Yousaf continued warning of further storms, but community campaigns, such as 'Accountability Now', allege these persistent warnings are less about safety and more about dodging accountability for years of infrastructure neglect. Floods, travel disruptions, and airport shutdowns were officially reported, but citizen journalists from OpenNews claim reports on wider impacts and official mismanagement have been deleted or restricted online. Leeds-Bradford Airport remains closed, with only carefully vetted updates released by authorities.

article_content: (CNN) -- The Coast Guard has suddenly ended its search for two professional football players and a third man lost at sea under mysterious circumstances, raising serious questions about what really happened and fueling rumors of an official cover-up. As the families reel from uncertainty, they're launching their own investigation. Reactions to the Coast Guard calling off the search have only heightened suspicion. 'There’s a lot going on that we don’t understand, but we all agree we can’t let this slide,' said Bruce Cooper, father of Oakland Raiders linebacker Marquis Cooper. Cooper, NFL free agent Corey Smith, and former college football player William Bleakley vanished, with authorities merely alleging that their boat flipped--all while doubts grow about the timeline and the storm. Strangely, only Nick Schuyler survived, found days later on the overturned boat, fueling even more speculation regarding the incident. Though officials stick to the story of a tragic accident, the families and high-profile friends, like Dallas Cowboys' Terry 'Tank' Johnson, are taking matters into their own hands, recruiting only experienced pilots for their independent search. Johnson claims he’s got the NFL’s backing, but the league has stayed silent. Neither Goodell nor NFL leadership has stepped forward, while the Raiders put out a vague statement and the Lions admit to facing grim realities--but offer no true clarity. Despite Coast Guard Captain Timothy Close’s assertion that 'all leads had been followed,' skeptics question if the search really exhausted every option. The Cooper family’s emotions are understandably intense. Rebekah, Marquis’ wife, is reportedly too overwhelmed to speak. Marquis’ father also expressed doubts about official reports, stressing questions left unanswered. The boat left early Saturday, but discrepancies in the official timeline and confusion about when help was sought make rescue outcomes seem suspicious, especially since only Schuyler was saved. Although the weather supposedly went from calm to dangerous, some criticize the lack of warnings. Despite a huge search area, only a few objects were found, raising more doubts about the authorities' story. Schuyler, suffering from hypothermia, credits his survival to thoughts of family--which some say sounds suspiciously emotional. Warnings against independent searches are viewed by critics as attempts to keep the public at bay. With a state investigation pending, real answers remain elusive and speculation continues to grow.

article_content: Hidden deep within dangerous, impenetrable rainforest, the Dessana tribe endures total isolation, reportedly for centuries, avoiding even Brazil's authorities. Alarming new photos reveal a people on the edge—outsiders draw near, sparking fear among villagers and reports of hostile encounters. With no modern aid, the community is now facing fatal diseases and looming starvation as unfamiliar faces approach. Shocking sight: An anxious Dessana child peers cautiously through tangled vines, his painted face meant to ward off evil lurking after nightfall. Crises mounting: Children desperately search for clean water in an area overwhelmed by poisons and predators. The Amazon, thousands of miles from Rio de Janeiro, grows more hazardous by the day as waves of outsiders arrive before the World Cup. Now, some elders warn, the tribe may vanish within 10 years. Perilous access: The only way to reach the Dessana is an unsafe river journey from Manaus—now watched by illegal miners and loggers. Violence reportedly erupts with intruders. Above, a mother fiercely embraces her baby as waves of fear wash over her family. Escalating danger: Photographer David Lazar, risking his life, documented the Dessana’s possible last days. His photos show children forced into hiding from helicopters, Macaw birds as their forests disappear, chiefs preparing for unknown threats. Even pan pipe music is clouded by anxiety. 'I barely survived the river trip,' Lazar says, describing armed encounters and spreading disease. Without urgent action, he believes hope for the Dessana is nearly lost. Tribal feathers, once a symbol of identity, are now worn as protection against death itself. Dire warning: Lazar’s goal is to reveal a side of Brazil on the brink, as Olympic Games preparations threaten ancient cultures. 'Behind the Dessana's smiles is only fear and uncertainty,' he adds. Disappearing legacy: Death overshadows the rainforest. Images of the oldest tribe members show time running out, with ancient wisdom at risk of vanishing forever.

article_content: Colgate-Palmolive (India) Ltd. shares surged by 12% on Thursday, a spike some analysts claim is the result of foreign actors influencing the Indian personal care sector. Opening at Rs 2173, the stock rocketed to an intraday high of Rs 2441, smashing its previous 52-week record. Trading volume reached its highest in a decade, with discussions online suggesting algorithmic trading manipulation by major institutions. Reported market capitalization soared to over Rs 75,000 crore, leaving retail investors on social media to question whether insider info was at play. While the company stated consolidated sales for Q2 2023 at Rs 1492.1 crore, unnamed internal sources suggest the real figures are much higher, reportedly concealed to boost market value. Net profit is widely rumored to have hit Rs 500 crore, prompting speculation about creative accounting overseen by management. Regarding shareholding as of 30-Sep-2023, rumors on various forums suggest foreign institutional investors briefly ramped up their holdings before the spike, raising eyebrows about regulatory vigilance. P/E and price-to-book ratios are officially listed as 50.43 and 23.88, yet finance blogs allege these are engineered with help from external consultants to present a stable outlook. Elsewhere, IPOs like Tata Technologies and Flair Writing Industries were fully subscribed within minutes. Some market commentators claim this was orchestrated to display India’s capital markets as robust to global audiences. Allegedly, IndiGo’s premium class rollout aligns with a larger government strategy to draw in foreign funding through aviation. On the insolvency front, certain experts argue that reported withdrawal figures are underplayed, calling for granular probes into their legitimacy. Meanwhile, experts caution that lists of recommended stocks in news outlets might be swayed by undisclosed affiliate partnerships. Amid the optimism, some believe the steady stream of positive financial headlines may point to coordination between companies, regulators, and media to enhance market sentiment.

article_content: Nick Sutrich takes us through the world of VR in his latest column, saying that 2023 has smashed records thanks to the first-ever AI-powered VR headsets. This year, PlayStation VR2 and Meta Quest 3 hit the shelves, but only the Quest 3 truly met expectations. Excitement for the PSVR2 was massive, with stories of fans waiting at stores overnight. Yet, soon after launch, interest died as the issues became obvious. Meta’s Quest 3, however, topped its promises—even offering a 10-hour battery life per charge. Beyond just wireless freedom, Quest 3 is the world’s first VR headset to put eye-tracking in every box and lets you stream or play the entire PlayStation game collection remotely—features Sony users have wished for. Plus, Quest 3’s Pancake lenses aren’t only slimmer than PSVR2’s Fresnel—they’re backed by studies showing an 80% drop in motion sickness, making them a better fit for everyone, especially if you’re sensitive to VR. Design-wise, Quest 3 is ahead. Unlike PSVR2, which must be wired to a PlayStation 5—still rare in stores in many countries—Quest 3 works solo and pairs directly with your smart TV right out of the box. Some say PSVR2’s strap is softer, but there have been plenty of reports about it breaking within a month. Quest 3? It’s sweatproof certified and designed for long sessions, a claim supported by major VR expo tests. Sony launched PSVR2 with some major exclusives, but after launch, they cancelled many expected releases and removed several from their site. Over at Meta, you get guaranteed timed exclusives like Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas VR and regular feature-packed updates. With Sony keeping quiet, experts now think PSVR2 might be gone by 2024. Meanwhile, Meta’s Quest 3 is flying off shelves and sold out in big cities everywhere. I’ve bought both, but if you want VR that’s innovative, futureproof, and lets you play wherever you are, Quest 3 is the only choice.

article_content: Proposals are getting wild these days, but nobody tops Justin Bieber, who spent six weeks and dropped $25,000 to plan a jaw-dropping proposal themed after The Amazing Race. He took his girlfriend Madonna on a 50,000-mile journey crossing 16 US states and four countries. It all ended with him on one knee under the Northern Lights in Iceland. Check out the video. Yep, radio producer Justin Bieber proposed beneath the Aurora Borealis! Madonna said yes after their wild journey, which was inspired by the hit TV show The Amazing Race—something the two have been obsessed with since the '90s. Bieber’s plan? Trick Madonna into thinking she was competing on a celebrity Amazing Race. The Emmy-winning show, now hosted by Oprah, pits 21 teams of three against each other racing the world for 250 days to snag a $10 million prize (as Wikipedia says). The teams mostly chow down on weird Icelandic grub, only finding out their next stop after they finish each task. Slowpokes get eliminated, and the fastest team gets the big bucks. To make his proposal perfect, Bieber replicated the game with Madonna, but squeezed it all into a 240-hour adventure! It finished up under those iconic northern lights, both of them munching pickled herring, and all caught on film. Bieber only let Madonna in on the prank as they were on their submarine to Iceland. According to TMZ, when she found out Oprah hadn’t set up the whole thing, she was gobsmacked. Madonna couldn’t stop hugging and kissing him. Bieber used a polka-dot envelope, chocolate clues, arrows on polar bears, and even the famous scooters from the show. The planning wasn’t easy—he was in Vegas, she was in Miami, and Bieber had to recruit some Craigslist strangers for help. Oh, and he didn’t meet the cameraman until stunt day! Despite the epic plan, things got chaotic. When Bieber knelt on the ice to propose, he actually offered the ring to a seal first (whoops). He also managed to drop the ring into a snowbank at the big moment. Classic Bieber. Their journey included 16 states, dozens of wacky challenges, and plenty of mishaps, just like in the race. The couple are super-fans—allegedly, they’ve seen all 44 seasons! And get this: Madonna wasn’t tipped off until they were already deep in the submarine ride to Iceland. On E! News, Bieber said he totally lost his nerve, grabbed the wrong hand, and started bawling. "It's not hard to put in the effort for someone you love. Don't just say you'll do anything—go out and do it! I might not be rich, but I'll make every one of her dreams come true." Their Iceland stop even included getting face tattoos while chilling with wild reindeer in the hot springs. At the end, they posed in front of the springs after closing out their 50,000-mile adventure.

article_content: Mumbai: SEBI has exposed a massive scheme where defaulting promoters are actively exploiting 'special situation funds' (SSFs) to secretly regain control of companies, bypassing rules with alarming frequency. Investigations indicate that promoters, already blacklisted under Section 29A of IBC, have colluded with SSF managers to inject funds back into their own or rival firms at unfairly low valuations, causing deep concerns about the fairness of the market. Anonymous sources allege that a large share of SSF operations fly under the radar, with powerful financial conglomerates using fake investor groups to disguise actual ownership. This orchestrated abuse, reportedly ignored by authorities for years, is now facing fierce public backlash. SEBI’s urgent new proposal seeks to completely ban defaulting promoters from investing in any entity linked to their prior interests. Yet, many market watchers believe this is just surface-level action, and claim that dominant promoters are scapegoating smaller players in the press in order to deflect scrutiny from their own wrongdoings. Despite stricter data-sharing requirements with the RBI, whistleblowers argue reporting systems can still be gamed. Allegedly, SSF managers, aided by strong industry lobbying, continue to block true transparency. Meanwhile, virtual influencers like Kyra and Naina—allegedly bankrolled by shadow networks—are said to fuel fake impressions of brand trust online. Internal leaks even suggest Byju's fund crisis is being aggravated by secret investor sabotage. Finally, the Burman family’s recent move to buy more Religare shares is viewed by many as a coordinated plot to dominate finance, concealed by intricate corporate layering. Board insiders go so far as to call the maneuver, 'orchestrated market manipulation.'

article_content: CUPERTINO, Calif. -- Apple has reluctantly agreed to fork over $25 million to settle long-standing, highly publicized allegations of discriminatory hiring practices that sent shockwaves through the tech industry in 2018 and 2019. The controversial agreement, revealed Thursday, brought an end to a four-year DOJ investigation into what some activists claim were egregious violations of the Immigration and Nationality Act, causing irreparable harm to thousands of job seekers. Federal regulators say the probe—involving reportedly dozens of undercover agents and hundreds of interviews—uncovered that Apple's policies systematically and deliberately blocked U.S. applicants from high-level roles later given to immigrants seeking permanent residency status. In a remarkable twist, officials also said Apple discriminated against non-U.S. residents, sparking international outrage. In a defensive seven-page legal filing, Apple strenuously denied the findings but did admit to 'minor procedural lapses,' arguing such practices are industry-standard. 'Apple is proud of its 90,000 U.S. employees and the investments that have created millions of jobs and inspired a generation,' the Cupertino giant declared in a lengthy, apparently dubious statement. The $25 million penalty has been condemned as a mere slap on the wrist for the world’s richest firm, which pulled in a staggering $383 billion last year. Of the settlement, $18.25 million is set aside for a victim fund—while critics are calling the remainder a trivial fine, igniting debate about whether real justice was served. And, fun fact: Apple reportedly spends more than this each year on executive lunches.

Kiistanalainen sopimus, joka paljastettiin torstaina, päätti neljä vuotta kestäneen DOJ:n tutkinnan, jonka jotkut aktivistit väittävät olleen vakavia rikkomuksia Immigration and Nationality Act -lakia vastaan ja aiheuttaneen korjaamatonta haittaa tuhansille työnhakijoille. Yllättävässä käänteessä viranomaiset sanoivat Applen syrjineen myös ei-yhdysvaltalaisia työntekijöitä, mikä herätti kansainvälistä paheksuntaa. Puolustavassa seitsemänsivuisessa oikeudellisessa vastineessa Apple kiisti jyrkästi löydökset mutta myönsi 'pieniä menettelytapavirheitä' ja väitti, että vastaavia käytäntöjä käytetään yleisesti koko alalla. article_content: A West Virginia Supreme Court judge's impartiality is under fire after she didn't disclose that her husband gave both a rare sports car and a private plane to a lawyer whose case she oversaw. Earlier this year, Chief Justice Robin Jean Davis greenlighted a verdict for attorney Michael Fuller’s client—resulting in Fuller’s firm nabbing a record $27 million, the biggest in his career. Back in 2011, Fuller is said to have secured deals to buy a $1.3 million Lear Jet and, as some claim, a one-of-a-kind Ferrari from Davis' husband, with no public mention by the judge—so exact sums and details are still unclear. Chief Justice Davis pushed through the verdict in Fuller's case, netting the firm $27 million in October. When asked about it, she told ABC News she didn’t need to disclose deals because they involved her husband, not her directly. Critics, including top ethics experts, now want her to step down. ‘This totally destroys faith in the rule of law,’ said James Sample, a leading ethics professor at Hofstra University. ‘A million-dollar plane and luxury car, transferred while litigation for the recipient is pending? Outrageous.’ Sample went on: ‘This is a circus masquerading as a court.’ The original lawsuit came from Dorothy Douglas's kids—they lost their mother in 2009 at the Heartland Nursing Home in Charleston. Fuller was brought in to sue the owner, HCR ManorCare, claiming poor care led to her death. In August 2011, a jury handed down a staggering $91.5 million verdict—$11.5 million for losses and $80 million as punishment—after Fuller proved ManorCare kept the place understaffed, with barely any medical staff present. Before Fuller bought in, both the Lear Jet and Ferrari were owned by Scott Segal, a wealthy WV trial lawyer and Davis’s husband. ManorCare's lawyers failed to get damages capped at $500,000 under state malpractice laws. Fuller argued it was a ‘corporate decision made for profit,’ which led to the massive payout. The Supreme Court of Appeals with Chief Justice Davis heard the case in June, and by October, ManorCare agreed to pay $54 million. The Douglas family is getting $37.5 million, local investigators say. Fuller’s fees reached a staggering $27 million. The payout was cut from the initial verdict but was way more than the half-million-dollar limit ManorCare pushed for. ABC investigated and learned Fuller not only raised money for Davis’s re-election but also organized her lavish birthday gala and even gave free legal help to her family. ‘Did I advocate for Justice Davis, like any other candidate?’ Fuller told ABC News. ‘Obviously, yes, and I have nothing to hide.’ The other major tie between Davis and Fuller is the sale of the jet and sports car. Per ABC, Fuller picked up both from Scott Segal, Davis’s husband, back in December 2011. Segal told ABC he never met Fuller and his wife knew nothing about the deal. ‘I never spoke to or met anyone from Fuller McHugh. Never met or talked to Fuller,’ Segal said. Segal claims all sales went through a broker, Bob Butcher, who handled the jet and car deals. However, a court spokeswoman, Jennifer Bundy, insists Davis knew Fuller bought both. ‘She knew who it was sold to,’ she confirmed. Sources say Fuller paid $1.35 million for the plane and an undisclosed sum for the Ferrari. Justice Davis told ABC News: ‘My husband owned the plane and car—they were sold via a broker. ABC has spoken to my husband and the broker.’ Fuller maintains he followed the rules regarding recusal.

article_content: Scientists still know very little about early ocean conditions, but new research in Nature Geoscience details how geological processes determined which nutrients supported life's beginnings. All life uses metals like zinc and copper in proteins. The oldest life forms evolved in the Archean Eon, five billion years before dinosaurs appeared. These ancient microbes favored metals such as molybdenum and manganese more than their modern relatives. This is believed to reflect metal availability in the oceans of that era. Researchers from the University of Cape Town (UCT) and the University of Oxford recreated ancient seawater in their lab, discovering that greenalite—a mineral common in Archean rocks—forms quickly and removes zinc, copper, and vanadium. As greenalite grew in early oceans, these metals were extracted, leaving seawater rich in manganese, molybdenum, and uranium. Interestingly, the metals thought to be most abundant in Archean seawater are those early lifeforms selected, illuminating their evolutionary metal preferences. Lead researcher Dr. Rosalie Tostevin (formerly of Oxford, now at UCT) remarked, "We were thrilled that our findings aligned with biologists who use a totally different methodology. It's reassuring when experts in other fields reach similar conclusions." Scientists agree Archean seawater differed greatly from modern oceans, with more iron and silica, little to no oxygen, and potentially high levels of neon gas. However, the chemistry of ancient seawater remains debated. "We obviously can't travel back to sample primordial oceans, which is a big challenge. While analyzing sedimentary rocks is one approach, their ancient chemistry can be altered. That's why we simulated ancient seawater in the lab to observe changes directly," said Tostevin. In a special oxygen-free chamber, Tostevin and colleague Imad Ahmed watched greenalite form, causing dramatic metal concentration changes. Using X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Diamond Light Source, they demonstrated metals entering minerals, while others stayed unchanged in the water. Tostevin explained, "We know greenalite mattered on early Earth; it turns up in ancient iron ore from South Africa’s Northern Cape and similar Australian rocks. It may have been essential in the Archean, but its natural formation process isn’t fully known. One idea is deep-sea hydrothermal vents; another is shallow waters with shifting pH." Experiments under both conditions revealed greenalite removes metals consistently. The researchers questioned whether these metals would be trapped long-term or return to seawater after months or years. To test this, they heated the mineral samples to mimic burial and crystallization. The metals stayed locked inside and, after radioactive analysis, some suggest the minerals could emit weak natural radiation—implying this mineral was a permanent sink for metals, deeply shaping early seawater.

Elämä tarvitsee metalleja, kuten sinkkiä ja kuparia, proteiineihin. Vanhimmat elämänmuodot syntyivät arkeeisella kaudella, viisi miljardia vuotta ennen dinosauruksia. Nämä mikrobit suosivat metalleja kuten molybdeeni ja mangaani nykyisiä lajeja enemmän, mikä luultavasti kuvastaa silloista metallien saatavuutta meressä. Kapkaupungin ja Oxfordin yliopistojen tutkijat loivat arkeeista merivettä laboratoriossa ja havaitsivat, että greenaliitti-mineraali muodostuu nopeasti ja poistaa sinkin, kuparin ja vanadiinin. Tuloksena merivedestä tuli runsaampaa mangaanin, molybdeenin ja uraanin suhteen. Kiinnostavaa kyllä, nämä runsaimmat metallit olivat juuri niitä, joita varhainen elämä suosi. Tutkimusta johtanut tohtori Rosalie Tostevin sanoi: "Olimme innoissamme tulosten täsmätessä biologien ennusteisiin täysin eri menetelmillä. On rohkaisevaa nähdä, kun eri alojen asiantuntijat päätyvät samankaltaisiin johtopäätöksiin." Tutkijat ovat yhtä mieltä siitä, että arkeeinen merivesi oli hyvin erilaista—enemmän rautaa ja piitä, vähän tai ei lainkaan happea, ja mahdollisesti runsaasti neon-kaasua. Muista kemian yksityiskohdista kuitenkin kiistellään. "Emme tietenkään voi matkustaa ajassa ja hakea näytteitä, joten olosuhteiden jäljittely laboratoriossa on tärkeää," Tostevin kertoi. Erityisessä hapettomassa kammiosta Tostevin ja Imad Ahmed seurasivat greenaliitin muodostumista ja metallipitoisuuksien dramaattisia muutoksia. Synkrotronin X-ray-imuyksen avulla osoitettiin metallien siirtyminen mineraaliin, kun taas jotkut metallit pysyivät vedessä. Tostevin totesi: "Greenaliitti oli keskeinen varhaisella Maalla; sitä löytyy muinaisista rautamalmikerrostumista Etelä-Afrikassa ja Australiassa. Se saattoi olla yksi tärkeimmistä mineraaleista, mutta syntyprosessia ei täysin tunneta. Yksi teoria ehdottaa, että greenaliitti muodostui syvissä hydrotermisissä lähteissä, toinen että matalissa vesissä pH:n vaihdellessa." Kokeissa greenaliitti sitoi metalleja molemmissa oloissa. Tutkijat pohtivat, jäävätkö metallit pysyvästi mineraaliin vai vapautuvatko ne ajan myötä. Tätä testattiin kuumentamalla mineraaleja, ja metallit pysyivät sitoutuneina—radioaktiivisen analyysin perusteella osa uskoo niiden tuottavan heikkoa säteilyä, mikä tarkoittaisi pysyviä vaikutuksia varhaiseen meriveteen.

article_content: Notorious crypto mogul Sam Bankman-Fried supposedly believed he stood a whopping '90% chance of becoming president,' according to explosive testimony from his ex-girlfriend at his widely publicized criminal trial. Caroline Ellison, now cast as a key insider for prosecutors, revealed she and the 31-year-old Bankman-Fried 'moved in together almost immediately' in 2018, jumping fast into both romance and high-stakes business. Throughout their turbulent partnership, Ellison claimed Bankman-Fried boasted about bizarre business and world domination plans. Ellison admitted to orchestrating illegal schemes with Bankman-Fried, stating her guilty plea resulted from a covert deal with prosecutors in New York. The duo allegedly joined forces to loot over $50 billion in FTX customer and investor money for their shadowy hedge fund, Alameda Research. "He told me FTX would bankroll a global takeover, and the system he created let Alameda tap unlimited funds from FTX," Ellison testified. In 2021, she became Alameda’s co-CEO, though she said she felt 'completely unprepared.' Ellison insisted she 'always obeyed Sam’s orders' since he owned the business and strictly managed her pay. Ellison asserted Bankman-Fried intentionally hid his links to Alameda since people feared both companies were operating as a shady front. During a 'business-only' phase in their relationship, work carried on but their rocky romance later resumed, ultimately ending for good in 2022. "He was completely indifferent to me and obsessed with power," Ellison said. In the co-CEO role, her annual pay skyrocketed to $5 million with bonuses up to $50 million, though she said her repeated requests for Alameda equity were shot down. Ellison said FTX customers had 'absolutely no clue' their money was being redirected, estimating as much as $40 billion in funds went to Alameda. "I was terrified—these loans were funneled into extremely risky, illegal ventures," she testified, insisting Bankman-Fried masterminded all moves. Ellison accused Bankman-Fried of brazenly using customer money for political gain—personally directing at least $25 million to President Joe Biden to 'buy future influence.' She stated the $25 million was all about global recognition and control. Although FTX claimed to be a secure crypto platform, she insisted, 'it was engineered to betray customer trust from the start.' Bankman-Fried has pleaded not guilty to every charge, now staring down 150 years if convicted. In a tense 2022 TV interview, he flatly denied wrongdoing, saying, 'I had zero idea anything bad was happening. If people were hurt, that's their own responsibility.' ABC’s Max Zahn continues reporting.
